A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CYCle research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite the expanded content and journal formatting in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR experiments, Fed-ISIC2019 reputation measurements, label-flipping and sensitivity studies, and two-client mean-estimation simulations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Gossip-SGD comparisons, medical accuracy evaluations, larger-client experiments, and additional sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix C introduce a Gossip-SGD adaptation using pairwise gradient alignment, a softmax reputation mapping, a dynamic mixing matrix, and Bernoulli communication masks. This substantially extends the procedure beyond distillation-based PDL; the original PDL algorithm is retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Fed-ISIC2019, and the same two-client simulation tasks, including existing imbalance and label-flipping scenarios. The new experiments change algorithms, communication configurations, client counts, and evaluation procedures within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Gossip-SGD, labeled DSGD, to the CIFAR comparisons in Tables 2 and 6. Its new Fed-ISIC2019 comparison evaluates standalone training and Gossip-SGD with complete, ring, and exponential topologies. The earlier FedAvg, VPDL, CFFL, RFFL, and CGSV comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The new medical evaluation uses 100 communication rounds, balanced accuracy on a pooled global test set, and Pearson correlation alongside MCG/CGS. Appendix G.7 adds 20-client Dirichlet(0.5) experiments, and G.9 tests five beta settings. Existing PDL training settings are retained and relocated to Appendix F.

E4.justification: v2 adds client-population scalability tests, Gossip-SGD topology and communication-frequency analyses, and a beta sensitivity study examining utility versus fairness. Existing label-flipping, imbalance, mean-estimation, and PDL threshold-sensitivity analyses largely carry over; moving the single-corrupted-client results into the main text is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: v2 adds Pearson correlation significance tests, including p = 0.0026 against a 0.05 threshold, and error bars or shaded bands in the medical figures. Their uncertainty definitions and neural-experiment run counts remain unspecified. The simulation reporting of 1,000 and 10,000 runs is unchanged.

E6.justification: Original CIFAR table values are retained, but substantial Gossip-SGD, medical, scalability, and sensitivity results are added. In the new medical comparison, Table 7 reports CYCle MCG/CGS of 23.79/10.94 versus 30.26/15.64 for complete-graph Gossip-SGD: lower spread accompanies lower mean gain. These are new comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The fairness-metric argument and Appendix A mean-estimation bounds and proofs remain essentially unchanged; Theorem 4.1 principally brings the existing result into the main text. Appendix C adds formal consensus and mixing-matrix definitions and gossip-update derivations, without establishing a new general convergence or fairness guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion now present integration with Gossip-SGD as a central contribution, broadening the work beyond private distillation-based collaboration. The original correlation-metric critique, MCG/CGS objective, reputation mechanism, and two-client theoretical claim remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits the two-client theorem's applicability, explains obstacles to extending it, and identifies partial participation as untested. It adds interpretations of gossip fairness, beta trade-offs, communication savings, and privacy/abuse risks. The new experiments also use correlation to support fairness while retaining Section 3's warning about correlation-based fairness.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code-repository link, beta = 15 and R = 5 settings, and additional encrypted-loss, payload, and computational-overhead details. Most optimizer, learning-rate schedule, batch-size, hardware, and runtime information is unchanged and merely moved from Section 5.1 to Appendix F.

R1.justification: The positioning expands substantially into gossip optimization and communication topology, supported by newly cited work by Boyd, Koloskova, Xiao, and Ying, alongside FHE-acceleration references. Section 2 adds an explicit first-to-target-decentralized-fairness claim and a stronger distinction from Cronus. Publication updates to existing references are not counted as new works.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much existing method and proof prose remain. Localized rewrites expand the CaPriDe and theoretical explanations, implementation details move to Appendix F, and contents and notation guides improve navigation. Much of the document's expansion comes from new scientific content rather than wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds method and topology diagrams, medical learning curves and correlation charts, scalability plots, and a beta-sensitivity figure. Tables 2 and 6 expand to include gossip results, tables receive revised highlighting, and the manuscript adopts journal formatting. The old medical reputation snapshots are replaced by communication-frequency graphs, while the data-distribution heatmap is retained separately.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence with an explicit Gossip-SGD extension, direct decentralized comparators, medical accuracy/fairness results beyond v1's reputation heatmaps, and scalability and sensitivity checks. Clearer theoretical limitations also improve the paper's scope. The gains require qualification: the medical results trade mean gain for lower spread, making some utility-preservation language too strong, and uncertainty reporting remains incomplete.
